findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the collapse-stamp edit target: name outbound_mutation_builders.py (call sites :81 create-path and :276 update-path) in Scope as the site to invoke the rebar-type: stamp diff, rather than outbound_differ.py which only re-exports _diff_status_annotation_labels.
evidence: Plan: 'Invoke the type-stamp diff from outbound_differ.py at the same site the status stamp is threaded.'
search: `_diff_status_annotation_labels(` matches only outbound_mutation_builders.py:81 and :276; outbound_differ.py:79 is an import re-export.
outbound_differ.py:35/74 comments: mutation-building 'only by the extracted outbound_mutation_builders module; re-exported here'
Scope names outbound_differ.py but not outbound_mutation_builders.py
findings.finding: The plan locates the type-stamp diff invocation in outbound_differ.py ('invoke the type-stamp diff from outbound_differ.py at the same site the status stamp is threaded'), but the status stamp diff (_diff_status_annotation_labels) is not called in outbound_differ.py — that file only re-exports it (line 79). The real call sites are outbound_mutation_builders.py:81 (outbound-create path) and :276 (update path), a module produced by the cited f1bc split. outbound_mutation_builders.py is absent from the Scope list, so the actual edit target for the collapse round-trip stamp is unenumerated.
findings.location: Approach → 'Collapse round-trip (B2)'; Scope (lists outbound_differ.py for 'invoke the type stamp')
scenarios: Author edits outbound_differ.py expecting a stamp call site and finds only a re-export, missing the two real sites (create + update) in outbound_mutation_builders.py
The update-path site (:276) is a distinct call from the create-path site (:81); a single edit misses one direction of the round trip
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'outbound_differ.py — invoke the type stamp' with 'outbound_mutation_builders.py — invoke the rebar-type: stamp diff at both status-stamp sites (create :81, update :276)', and keep outbound_differ.py in scope only for the per-project skip threading.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend B4 to thread the per-project effective excluded set (config.effective_excluded_types) into BOTH the absent-GET pre-selection (_compute_outbound_select_absent_gets) AND the per-ticket main-loop exclusion check at outbound_differ.py:430, since the single project-blind frozenset at :377 feeds both.
evidence: Plan: 'Thread the ticket's project key ... into _compute_outbound_select_absent_gets'
search: excluded_sync_types consumed at outbound_differ.py:382 (pre-select), :430 (main loop, per-ticket `ticket.get("ticket_type") in excluded_sync_types`), :491/:519 (helper)
The main-loop check at :430 is not named in B4
findings.finding: The B4 per-project skip threading names only _compute_outbound_select_absent_gets as the consumer of the effective excluded set, but excluded_sync_types is also read at the per-ticket main-mutation-loop check (outbound_differ.py:430) and inside the helper (:491/:519). Since the skip set becomes per-project (per-ticket), the main-loop site at :430 must also consult the project-effective set rather than the single project-blind frozenset loaded once at :377.
scenarios: A skip-mapped type is excluded from absent-GET pre-selection but still emits mutations in the main loop because :430 uses the project-blind frozenset

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the B3 scope: register 'rebar-type:' in the THIRD independent prefix copy at inbound_collection_diffs.py:88 (the one inbound_differ re-exports and _diff_labels_inbound uses), not just outbound_labels.py:34 and inbound_translate.py:58 — the plan's 'exactly two edits' premise mis-identifies where inbound_differ's _EXCLUDED_PREFIXES originates.
evidence: Plan: 'the canonical tuple is outbound_labels._EXCLUDED_PREFIXES (outbound_labels.py:34), imported by outbound_differ and inbound_differ ... So B3 = exactly two edits'
inbound_differ.py:30-31 imports _EXCLUDED_PREFIXES from rebar_reconciler.inbound_collection_diffs (NOT from outbound_labels)
inbound_collection_diffs.py:88 defines an independent copy = ('rebar-id:','rebar-id-','imported:','rebar-status:')
inbound_collection_diffs.py:293-305 (_diff_labels_inbound) filters both jira_labels and local_tags by this copy; an unregistered rebar-type: label becomes a Jira-only tag -> inbound ADD
This is the exact spurious-mutation/tag-leak failure mode the plan's B3 regression guard and round-trip AC target
findings.finding: B3's excluded-prefix mechanism is incomplete: there are THREE independent _EXCLUDED_PREFIXES copies, not two. The plan misses inbound_collection_diffs.py:88, which is the copy inbound_differ actually re-exports and which _diff_labels_inbound uses to filter the inbound label diff. Without adding 'rebar-type:' there, the annotation label leaks into local tags as a spurious inbound ADD.
findings.location: Approach → 'Excluded-prefix registration (B3)'; AC line 4 (round-trip / no spurious tag mutation)
scenarios: A collapsed type stamps rebar-type: on the Jira issue; next inbound pass computes _diff_labels_inbound and emits an ADD, leaking rebar-type: into local ticket tags
test_type_collapse_roundtrip's 'no spurious tag REMOVE/ADD mutation' assertion fails, or passes only because the test never exercises the inbound label diff
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'rebar-type:' to all THREE copies: outbound_labels.py:34, inbound_collection_diffs.py:88, and inbound_translate.py:58. Restate B3 as three edits (or consolidate the three copies) and update the census/AC-4 accordingly.

evidence: Plan: 'Invoke the type-stamp diff from `outbound_differ.py` at the same site the status stamp is threaded.'
outbound_differ.py:76-80 imports `_diff_status_annotation_labels` with `# noqa: F401` (re-export only, no invocation).
outbound_mutation_builders.py:81 (create path) and :276 (update path) each call `_diff_status_annotation_labels(...)` — two threading sites, in a different module than the plan names.
findings.finding: The outbound type-stamp threading site is mislocated and under-counted. The plan says to invoke the type-stamp diff from `outbound_differ.py` 'at the same site the status stamp is threaded', but `_diff_status_annotation_labels` is not invoked in `outbound_differ.py` (which only re-exports it at line 79); it is threaded in `outbound_mutation_builders.py` at TWO distinct sites: the create path (line 81, `jira_labels=[]`) and the update path (line 276, `jira_labels=list(jira_fields...)`).

Patching only one of the two `outbound_mutation_builders.py` sites (e.g. create at l.81) leaves the UPDATE path (l.276) un-stamped, so a collapsed type on an already-bound ticket never gets its `rebar-type:` label refreshed, breaking the round-trip on update.
